title: What If Every Cat on Earth Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if every cat on Earth vanished tonight? Birds would notice first.
In the United States alone, free-ranging cats kill an estimated 1.3 to 4 billion birds every year.
They also kill an estimated 6 to 22 billion mammals a year, mostly small ones like mice and rats.
The deadliest are cats with no owner, such as barn cats and feral cats in cities.
Cats have also contributed to 33 modern extinctions, mostly on islands.
So your sofa cat is not the main culprit. Unowned cats cause most of it, and managing them could help birds the most.
